title: Paper Section Sorter
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: AI for EE Research
description: Classification activity in which learners place ten illustrative sentences from one invented engineering paper into one of six sections: Abstract, Introduction, Related work, Method, Results, or Discussion, by the reader question each sentence answers. Sentences come in a fixed order with one attempt each; every submission gets Correct or This belongs in feedback with a one-sentence reason, and the run ends with a score out of 10, a mastery statement at 8 of 10, and the sentences grouped by section.

educational.topic: Structure of an engineering research paper
learningObjectives: Classify each of ten sentences from an engineering paper into the section where it belongs, with at least 8 of 10 classified correctly
Explain a sentence's function by the reader question it answers
prerequisites: The sections of a paper and the reader question each answers, from the section Structure, Outline, and Abstract in Chapter 15

canvasDimensions.controlHeight: 44 to 116 (one to three rows of buttons, by width)

accessibility.notes: describe() provides a screen-reader description; all controls are native HTML buttons reachable with the Tab key and activated with Enter or Space; the chosen section button sets aria-pressed; keyboard focus moves to the next usable button after Submit and Next; correct and incorrect feedback uses words and check or X symbols as well as an Okabe-Ito color-blind-safe palette; all text is 16 px or larger.

controls.label: Abstract, Introduction, Related work, Method, Results, Discussion
controls.purpose: Six section buttons. Pressing one chooses that section for the current sentence; the choice can be changed until Submit. Disabled after the sentence is submitted.

controls.label: Submit
controls.purpose: Enabled once a section is chosen. Commits the single attempt for the current sentence and shows the feedback.

controls.label: Next / See Score
controls.purpose: Enabled after a submission. Advances to the next sentence in the fixed order, and after sentence 10 shows the score and the sentences grouped by section.

controls.label: More Sections
controls.purpose: Shown only on the summary screen when the sentences grouped by section do not fit on one page; pages through the groups.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Forced six-way classification of sentences from one invented paper, with one attempt per item and immediate explanatory feedback
keyQuestions: Which reader question does this sentence answer?
commonMisconceptions: Any sentence with a number is a result
A contribution statement belongs only in the abstract
A limitation belongs in the conclusion and not in the discussion
assessmentOpportunities: At least 8 of 10 sentences classified correctly on the first attempt is evidence of mastery
Reading the table of sections is exploration and is not evidence
